questions.problem: Calculate the points where the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=12$ intersects the line $x=-4.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-4,$ we substitute $x=-4$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ (-4)^{2}-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ 16-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ -{y}^{2} & =12-16 \\ -{y}^{2} & =-4 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $x=-4$  at the points $(-4,\pm 2).$

questions.problem:
Calculate the points where the hyperbola
$\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}=1$
intersects the line $x=-4.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-4,$ we substitute $x=-4$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{8}-\frac{(-4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{8}-1 & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & =1+1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =16 \\ y & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line  $x=-4$ at the points $(-4,\pm 4).$

$$

$$

questions.problem:
In **ascending order,** the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $14{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}=64$ intersects the line $y=\sqrt{2}x$ are

$\,x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=\sqrt{2}x,$ we first replace $y$ with $\sqrt{2}x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}14{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2} & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-5(\sqrt{2}x)^{2} & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-5(2{x}^{2}) & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-10{x}^{2} & =64 \\ 4{x}^{2} & =64 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection are
$x=-4$ and $x=4.$
